nonrx_launch.label: Non-prescription line goes live (model month)
nonrx_launch.conf: Supplement line needs only manufacturing, label/claims review and a storefront. Conservative allows one month of slippage on label review.

rx_launch.label: Prescription telehealth line goes live (model month)
rx_launch.conf: Requires the provider agreement, physician entity, pharmacy contracts, LegitScript certification and a state-by-state licensure map. Benchmark B10, B11.

followers.label: Proposed brand partner Instagram followers
followers.conf: Third-party trackers report 27,410,219 as of June 2026 (range 27.0M-28.3M). Benchmark B16. Held constant across scenarios because it is measured, not chosen. NOT an audited or first-party figure.

posts_per_month.label: Brand posts per month by the partner (feed plus reels)
posts_per_month.conf: A contract deliverable, not a market variable. Set to whatever the agreement actually obliges.

reach_pct.label: Reach per brand post as a share of followers
reach_pct.conf: Analyst assumption bounded by benchmark B15: the 10M-plus tier averages ~1.77% ENGAGEMENT; reach exceeds engagement but organic reach at this tier is heavily throttled and branded content more so. Reels reach higher than static.

ctr_reach.label: Click-through to site per reached impression
ctr_reach.conf: Analyst assumption. No tier-level link-click benchmark was retrievable (benchmark B15 notes this gap). This is the single least-evidenced driver in the model.

attn_decay.label: Monthly decay of partner-driven traffic toward a floor
attn_decay.conf: Analyst assumption. Celebrity launch demand spikes then settles; benchmark B14 notes IM8's founders deliberately did not rely on fame for durability.

attn_floor.label: Floor for partner-driven traffic as a share of the launch peak
attn_floor.conf: Analyst assumption. Represents the durable follower demand that persists after novelty.

launch_spike.label: Launch-month multiplier on partner-driven traffic
launch_spike.conf: Announcement window concentrates attention. Analyst assumption.

organic_m1.label: Organic and direct sessions, month 1
organic_m1.conf: New domain with an editorial library. Analyst assumption.

organic_growth.label: Organic monthly growth rate
organic_growth.conf: Content-led SEO compounding from a small base. Analyst inference.

organic_cap.label: Organic and direct sessions ceiling
organic_cap.conf: Caps compounding; category search demand is finite. Analyst inference.

paid_pre.label: Paid media per month before the non-Rx launch

paid_floor.label: Minimum paid media per month after launch
paid_floor.conf: Keeps a spend floor while revenue is small.

paid_pct.label: Paid media as a share of prior-month net revenue
paid_pct.conf: Benchmark B02: the closest listed telehealth comparable ran marketing at 35-40% of revenue. A celebrity-led brand should sit WELL below that, because the point of the partnership is that owned audience substitutes for bought audience; if this driver has to rise toward 35% the partnership is not working. Prior-month basis avoids a circular reference.

launch_push.label: One-time launch marketing and PR, non-Rx launch month
launch_push.conf: Announcement window spend. Deliberately modest: the point of a founder with a large audience is that the launch does not have to be bought. A brand spending heavily here is paying twice for the same attention.

paid_cap.label: Maximum paid media per month
paid_cap.conf: A budget ceiling and a backstop. Diminishing returns and the fulfilment capacity ramp now do most of the work of bounding growth, so this is set high enough that the percent-of-revenue rule governs rather than the cap. At the Aggressive ceiling it is roughly 27% of revenue at scale, in line with benchmark B02.

paid_elast.label: Paid response elasticity (sessions per marginal dollar)
paid_elast.conf: Diminishing returns on the cold prospecting tier. Sessions scale as (spend / reference spend) raised to this power, so at ten times the reference the effective cost per session rises about 1.8x at 0.74. Below 1.0 is the whole point: auction competition and audience exhaustion mean the second million never buys what the first did. Analyst assumption, standard media-mix practice.

bsearch_per_reach.label: Branded searches generated per reached impression
bsearch_per_reach.conf: Each brand post sends some viewers to a search engine rather than to the link. Analyst assumption; no tier-level benchmark was retrievable. This is the mechanism by which celebrity promotion creates cheap paid inventory rather than just free traffic.

bsearch_organic_factor.label: Branded and intent searches per organic session
bsearch_organic_factor.conf: Baseline brand-name and category-intent search that exists independently of the partner. Analyst assumption.

bsearch_capture.label: Share of available branded and intent search bought
bsearch_capture.conf: You cannot buy every query, and you should not: some arrive free through organic listings. Analyst assumption.

cps_search.label: Cost per session, branded and intent search
cps_search.conf: Branded queries are the cheapest paid inventory a brand owns because it faces little auction competition on its own name. Analyst assumption anchored to health-category CPC proxies.

conv_mult_search.label: Conversion multiplier, branded and intent search
conv_mult_search.conf: High-intent traffic converts well above the site average. Analyst assumption; no branded-search multiplier benchmark was retrievable (B19 notes the gap).

search_increment.label: Share of branded-search conversions that are incremental
search_increment.conf: THE HONEST HAIRCUT. Paying for a query you would rank for organically buys a click you already had. Benchmark B19 makes the same point about retargeting. Without this factor the model would double-count the partner's organic traffic and the paid search that harvests it.

retarget_pool_sessions.label: Share of prior-month sessions addressable for retargeting
retarget_pool_sessions.conf: Cookie and consent loss, app-tracking opt-outs and platform matching all shrink the pool. Analyst assumption.

retarget_pool_engagers.label: Partner-post engagers addressable per reached impression
retarget_pool_engagers.conf: People who engaged with a brand post can be retargeted from the platform's engagement audience. This is the second mechanism by which the partnership creates cheap, warm ad inventory. Analyst assumption bounded by benchmark B15: the 10M-plus tier averages about 1.77% engagement.

retarget_freq.label: Sessions bought per addressable pool member per month
retarget_freq.conf: How hard the warm pool is worked before fatigue. Analyst assumption.

cps_retarget.label: Cost per session, retargeting
cps_retarget.conf: Warm audiences cost less per click than cold. Benchmark B19: retargeting CPA runs 40-70% below cold acquisition.

conv_mult_retarget.label: Conversion multiplier, retargeting
conv_mult_retarget.conf: Benchmark B19: retargeting ROAS averages about 4.2x against 1.5-3x for cold prospecting, roughly 71% higher.

retarget_increment.label: Share of retargeting conversions that are incremental
retarget_increment.conf: THE SECOND HONEST HAIRCUT, and the one most often ignored. Benchmark B19: holdout tests show true incremental lift of 25-30%, meaning up to 75% of retargeting conversions would have happened anyway. Retargeting mostly harvests demand that the partner's organic posts and the prospecting tier already created.

cps_prospect.label: Cost per session, cold prospecting, generic creative
cps_prospect.conf: Health and wellness CPC proxies; restricted-category ad review raises cost. LegitScript certification is a precondition for scaled healthcare advertising (benchmark B10). Instagram feed ad click-through commonly 0.22-0.88% (B20).

creative_disc.label: Cost-per-session discount from partner creative
creative_disc.conf: A recognisable face and partner-voiced video should raise click-through and so lower cost per session. NO celebrity-specific benchmark was retrievable; the supporting evidence is only general (video creative 30-50% higher click-through, faces in visuals recommended) per B20. Treat as an analyst assumption, and note that using the partner's likeness in PAID media needs broader licensing than organic posting and faces additional health-category ad review.

conv_mult_prospect.label: Conversion multiplier, cold prospecting
conv_mult_prospect.conf: The reference tier. Held at 1.0 by definition so the other multipliers are read relative to cold traffic.

conv_mult_partner_organic.label: Conversion multiplier, the partner's own organic traffic
conv_mult_partner_organic.conf: Followers arriving from a brand post are warmer than cold prospects but colder than someone searching the brand by name. Analyst assumption.

rx_celeb_factor.label: Prescription-intent factor on partner-driven and cold-prospecting traffic
rx_celeb_factor.conf: A follower who clicks a supplement post is much less likely to start a prescription consult than someone who searched for peptide therapy. The partner also cannot promote compounded prescription products, so prescription intent has to come from search, organic content and on-site cross-sell rather than from partner creative. Analyst assumption.

cap_m1.label: Orders the supply chain can ship in the first live month
cap_m1.conf: Manufacturing minimum order quantities, batch lead times, label print runs and 3PL onboarding all gate the first months. Demand above this ceiling is treated as LOST, not backlogged, which is the conservative treatment. Analyst assumption; replace with the contract manufacturer's actual run schedule.

cap_growth.label: Monthly growth in shippable capacity
cap_growth.conf: How fast production and fulfilment can be scaled. Binds hard in the first year of the Aggressive case and stops binding thereafter. Analyst assumption.

shop_conv.label: Order conversion rate, all sessions
shop_conv.conf: DTC supplement conversion commonly 0.5-1.5%; a warm follower audience should sit at the top of or above that band, but benchmark B15 warns mega-tier audiences convert worse than their reach implies.

nonrx_aov.label: Average order value
nonrx_aov.conf: Above the $30-65 monthly band in benchmark B06, reflecting a premium multi-product basket. Requires validation.

sub_attach.label: Share of new customers taking a subscription
sub_attach.conf: Subscribe-and-save attach on consumables. Analyst assumption.

sub_churn.label: Monthly subscription churn
sub_churn.conf: Benchmark B05: 4-7% monthly well run, 8-12% category average, 12-20% churning in month one alone.

onetime_repeat.label: Monthly reorder rate of one-time buyers
onetime_repeat.conf: Approximation: applied to the prior month's one-time cohort only, which understates a long tail and is deliberately conservative.

nonrx_cogs_pct.label: Landed product COGS as a share of retail
nonrx_cogs_pct.conf: Benchmark B03: landed COGS 20-30% of retail for DTC supplements, giving 70-80% product gross margin.

nonrx_fulfil.label: Pick, pack and ship per order (ambient)
nonrx_fulfil.conf: 3PL pick-pack plus domestic parcel. Ambient, not cold chain.

rx_intent.label: Eligibility-quiz start rate, all sessions
rx_intent.conf: Analyst assumption. Prescription intent is a small slice of brand traffic.

eligible_rate.label: Share of completions with a clinically eligible outcome
eligible_rate.conf: Red-flag screening removes a material share. Never a target; a safety control.

state_cov_launch.label: US population covered by served states at Rx launch
state_cov_launch.conf: Licensure, asynchronous-prescribing rules and corporate-practice-of-medicine limits gate this. Fifty-state prescription coverage is NOT available on day one.

state_cov_cap.label: Maximum covered population
state_cov_cap.conf: Some states stay excluded on asynchronous or CPOM grounds.

intake_submit.label: Intake submission rate, eligible to intake

rx_rate.label: Clinician prescribing rate
rx_rate.conf: A clinical decision, never a target. Observed telehealth ranges 50-70%. Monitored solely for safety and for evidence of undue influence.

enroll_rate.label: Paid enrolment rate after a prescription is issued
enroll_rate.conf: Price friction at the plan step; all-in pricing shown before intake improves this.

rx_churn.label: Monthly churn, prescription programmes
rx_churn.conf: Benchmark B17: ~65% discontinuation within 12 months in the comparable telehealth population, 84.4% by 24 months. THE most damaging driver if wrong.

rx_price.label: Programme price per member-month, blended
rx_price.conf: Benchmark B07: sermorelin $96-199 telehealth, tissue protocols $100-300, stacks $80-180, combinations $350-600.

consult_fee.label: Consultation fee charged at intake
consult_fee.conf: Benchmark B08: asynchronous visits price at $15-40 commonly, up to $60 for longer reviews. Charged whether or not a prescription follows; refunded if screened ineligible.

pharm_cost.label: Pharmacy medication cost per member-month
pharm_cost.conf: 503A compounded peptide cost to a telehealth sponsor, volume-tiered. Not independently verified; obtain a written tiered schedule.

consult_cost.label: Clinician cost per completed consult
consult_cost.conf: Benchmark B08 cites provider time around $30 per programme plus platform and support. One-time at enrolment.

refill_cost.label: Clinician cost per active member-month (monitoring and refill review)
refill_cost.conf: Recurring clinical review. Must be paid per unit of clinical work, never as a share of revenue.

coldchain_ship.label: Cold-chain fulfilment and shipping per fill
coldchain_ship.conf: Benchmark B09: $1.95 base pack rate plus cold storage, insulated mailers, gel packs and a 2-day temperature-controlled lane. The pack rate alone is NOT the landed cost.

rx_support.label: Non-clinical support cost per active member-month
rx_support.conf: Tooling plus staffed support per member.

pay_fee.label: Payment processing
pay_fee.conf: Card fees 2.7-3.2%. Healthcare and supplement merchants are frequently underwritten as elevated risk, which raises the rate and makes LegitScript certification close to a prerequisite (benchmark B10).

refund_pct.label: Refunds and chargebacks
refund_pct.conf: 2-5% typical. Auto-renewal programmes attract chargebacks; ROSCA-compliant cancellation reduces them.

provider_fee.label: Turnkey compliance and fulfilment provider, flat fee
provider_fee.conf: As specified by the project owner. Modelled as a PLATFORM fee only. Published market pricing for comparable turnkey telehealth infrastructure is $3,000-6,000/month plus $5,000-10,000 onboarding plus per-consult fees (benchmark B11), so a $600 fee is very unlikely to absorb medication, per-consult, cold-chain or processing costs. Those are carried separately above. See the Provider_Diligence sheet.

cert_cost.label: Certification and registrations per month
cert_cost.conf: Benchmark B10: ~$3,125 year one and ~$2,150/yr thereafter per site for LegitScript, plus state registrations and renewals; amortised monthly.

team_pre.label: Team per month before the non-Rx launch
team_pre.conf: Founder or GM plus fractional operations and contract creative. Small because the provider carries clinical and fulfilment operations. The Conservative column is deliberately a LEAN operator, not a normal operator with weak demand, so that the Conservative outcome reflects demand risk rather than an arbitrary spending choice.

team_p1.label: Team per month, non-Rx launch through month 12
team_p1.conf: A founder or general manager, one capable performance-media buyer, and part-time support. Deliberately small: the provider carries clinical operations, fulfilment and compliance administration, and the brand partner supplies much of the creative. A team larger than this is rebuilding in-house what the $600 fee already covers.

team_p2.label: Team per month, months 13-24
team_p2.conf: Scales with order volume and state count, but stays small relative to revenue because the provider carries clinical operations and fulfilment. A brand at this revenue running team above roughly 15% of net revenue has rebuilt in-house what it is already paying the provider for.

team_pct_floor.label: Team cost floor as a share of net revenue
team_pct_floor.conf: Flat headcount steps are the classic way a model overstates profitability at scale: a brand doing tens of millions a month cannot be run by the team that ran it at one million. Team cost is therefore the GREATER of the step above and this share of revenue. It does not bind at Conservative or Baseline volumes; it binds hard in the Aggressive case, which is the point.

creative_pct_floor.label: Creative and content floor as a share of net revenue
creative_pct_floor.conf: Same correction applied to production. Creative volume has to grow with spend or the ads fatigue; 2-3% of revenue is a modest allowance for a brand whose whole acquisition model is creative-led.

tech_pct_floor.label: Technology floor as a share of net revenue
tech_pct_floor.conf: Storefront, subscription, support, data and consent tooling all price on volume. Flat SaaS line items stop being flat.

med_lead.label: Medical director and clinical oversight per month
med_lead.conf: Fractional medical director retainer. Compensation must never vary with prescription volume or revenue.

tech.label: Technology and software per month
tech.conf: Storefront, subscription management, analytics, consent management, CRM, helpdesk. Separate from the provider fee.

legal_p0.label: Legal and regulatory per month, months 1-3
legal_p0.conf: Entity structure and MSO or friendly-PC review, provider agreement review, formulary eligibility opinion, claims and label review, endorsement and disclosure protocol, trademark, privacy. Front-loaded deliberately.

legal_ongoing.label: Legal and compliance per month thereafter
legal_ongoing.conf: Ongoing claims review, state expansion opinions, FDA list monitoring, contract maintenance.

insurance.label: Insurance per month from the non-Rx launch
insurance.conf: Product liability, professional, cyber and D&O. A vendor contract does not transfer the brand's own liability.

creative.label: Creative, content and organic social per month
creative.conf: Production the brand controls, distinct from paid media and from partner compensation. Materially lower than a comparable brand would spend, because a founder-partner posting several times a month supplies usable creative as a by-product. That saving is one of the concrete economic benefits of the partnership.

partner_cash.label: Partner cash retainer per month from the non-Rx launch
partner_cash.conf: Illustrative only. Structure, amount and mix are entirely unnegotiated. Conservative case models an equity-only deal with no cash retainer.

partner_royalty.label: Partner royalty on net revenue
partner_royalty.conf: Illustrative. Consumer-brand licensing royalties commonly 3-10%. Held flat across scenarios so the scenarios isolate business performance rather than deal terms.

partner_equity.label: Partner equity, fully diluted (reference only)
partner_equity.conf: Illustrative. Non-cash; shown on the Partner_Economics sheet for reference and NOT charged to EBITDA.

inv_months.label: Non-Rx inventory held, in months of COGS
inv_months.conf: Supplement manufacturing runs have long lead times and minimum order quantities, so inventory is the main working-capital draw. The Rx line carries no inventory; the pharmacy does.
